title: Paul Krugman Says AI Boom Is ‘Crowding Out’ Other Investments in a Way the Dot-Com Era Never Did: ‘This Isn’t a Hypothetical Risk’
source_used: Paul Krugman's Substack (also Benzinga on Yahoo Finance)
key_facts: Paul Krugman wrote on his Substack on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 that massive spending on data centres is crowding out investment in everything else.
He argues AI spending raises interest rates when the economy is near full employment, so other investment loses out.
He says the 1990s tech boom showed no crowding out because America attracted very large inflows of foreign investment, which is not happening now.
His charts show data centre construction diverting funds from housing, offices and factories.
He also points to data centres using scarce electricity and chip demand pushing up chip prices.
He says nobody can tell whether there is a bubble, and calls such predictions 'at best educated guesses', but warns private credit fallout may be larger than many realise.
Benzinga adds that JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon expects hyperscalers to spend nearly $1 trillion next year, up from about $700 billion.
quote_evidence: Massive spending on data centers is crowding out investment in everything else in the economy.
So it’s clear that crowding out by the AI boom is happening on a very large scale. And unlike the risks of technological unemployment or a burst bubble, this isn’t a hypothetical risk.
Surges in private spending, like the current immense AI boom, also drive up interest rates.
why_it_matters_hint: A Nobel-winning economist says the AI boom is already costing the wider economy through higher borrowing costs.
notes: Read Krugman's own Substack post and the Benzinga/Yahoo summary. Post is two days old by 8 Oct; score lowered by 1.
